name: Anomaly Cheat Sheet
short: Two pages: how to read funding rates, the price/OI matrix, and 7 rules that survive contact with the market.
long: The two-page version of everything I check before shorting an altcoin: how funding is actually paid, what a positive vs negative print means for the crowd, how price and open interest move together, and the seven rules I apply when a chart looks 'obvious'.
includes: Funding-rate table with the thresholds I actually use
Price/OI matrix — four quadrants in plain English
7 entry and exit rules, each with the reason behind it
One-page checklist for a second monitor
forWho: Traders who already place perpetual futures trades and want a reference sheet that fits on one screen.
notFor: Complete beginners — the sheet assumes you know what funding is and how a perp differs from spot.

name: Altcoin Anomaly Radar
short: Scans every USDT perpetual on Bitget, flags funding extremes, 24h moves, 5-minute spikes and OI jumps — with a plain-English read on each hit.
long: Scans every USDT perpetual on Bitget — around 800 contracts — and returns a short list of anomalies instead of a wall of charts: funding extremes, 24-hour moves, 5-minute spikes and open-interest jumps. Every hit comes with a one-line reason it was flagged, so you can dismiss it in two seconds or dig in.
includes: config file for thresholds and your watchlist
CSV/JSON export that drops into the journal
Written guide: how to read the output
forWho: Anyone watching more than 30 altcoin perps and tired of scrolling.
notFor: People looking for buy/sell signals or auto-trading — the radar only ranks what looks unusual.

name: Trade Review Journal
short: Log 10 fields per trade. It computes win rate, R-multiples, payoff ratio, max drawdown and draws your equity curve automatically.
long: A trade log that does the arithmetic you keep putting off. Ten fields per trade, and the workbook computes win rate, R-multiples, payoff ratio, max drawdown and an equity curve — then breaks the results down by setup and by mistake type, so patterns show up before they cost you again.
includes: Dashboard: win rate, R, payoff, drawdown, equity curve
Sample data sheet you can delete
forWho: Discretionary traders taking more than ~10 trades a month who want to know which setups actually pay.
notFor: Fully automated systems that already export their own statistics.

name: Both tools
short: The radar and the journal together — $6 cheaper than buying them separately.
long: Radar plus journal, $6 cheaper than buying them separately. The scanner narrows 800 contracts down to a handful; the journal tells you whether your execution on that handful is actually working. They share one export format, so the loop is: scan, trade, log, review.
includes: Shared CSV export so radar output drops straight into the journal
forWho: Traders who want the filter and the feedback loop in one purchase.
notFor: Anyone who only wants the reference sheet — buy the $5 PDF instead.
